page: Microsoft Azure D8d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The configuration includes 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 307 GB of local SSD storage. There are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses bundled with this instance.

Benchmark evaluations position the D8d_v4 consistently in the average tier across most metrics. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded scores of 1421.78 and 7443.02 respectively, while the Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores reached 1237.0 and 4751.0. Memory bandwidth tests showed 414.44 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 46.63 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-threaded gzip compression at 23.73 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 27.25 GB/sec performed in the weak tier, indicating potential bottlenecks for heavy data compression tasks.

This instance provides a balanced resource configuration suitable for general-purpose workloads, web serving, and database operations. It achieved 7.06 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a static web serving throughput of 6.77 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the server processed 449.52 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M LLM model. The inclusion of 307 GB of local storage offers qualitative cost efficiency for applications requiring temporary high-speed scratch space without the added expense of external storage attachments.

The hardware profile includes 32.0 GB of RAM and 307 GB of local storage, with no integrated GPUs.
